title: Fordham's 1941 Nehru text is where the sourcebook locates his language of non-alignment
summary: Fordham attributes the language of non-alignment to Nehru and prints his 1941 essay.
body: Fordham's headnote says Nehru, India's first prime minister after 1947, created terms such as neutralism, Third World, and non-alignment, and it prints his 1941 essay Marxism, Capitalism and India's Future. The headnote's claim that he created those terms is the sourcebook's attribution. The essay is his political argument, not a dictionary entry. The wording on the page includes: "independence, (1947) was the creator of such terms as "neutralism", "Third World", and "non-alignment". Marxism, Capitalism and India's Future (1941) As our struggle toned down and established itself at a low level, there was little of excitement in it, except at long intervals. My thoughts traveled more to other countries, and I watched and studied, as far". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
said_by: Jawaharlal Nehru, Fordham headnote and text
